signals.title_or_quote: How do you catch schema drift and security gaps in Firestore?
signals.why_relevant: Author describes schema drift between TypeScript types and runtime data — exactly the problem schemaguard solves.
signals.drafted_reply: Schema drift in Firestore is real — the root cause is usually that your TypeScript types and your runtime validation live in two separate files that nobody keeps in sync. One approach: generate validators directly from your existing interfaces at build time so there is only one source of truth. That is what schemaguard does — {APP_URL}. Disclosure: I built it. Even if you skip it, the key insight is to treat your TS types as the schema, not a parallel Zod file.

signals.title_or_quote: Validation pipeline that blocks AI-generated files with schema errors
signals.why_relevant: Author needs runtime schema validation for structured files — schemaguard compiles validators from TS types at build time.
signals.drafted_reply: For blocking malformed structured files, the most reliable approach is to derive your validator from the same TypeScript type that describes the expected shape — that way the validator can never drift from the spec. You can do this with a compiler plugin that emits a validator at build time. schemaguard ({APP_URL}) does exactly that. Disclosure: I'm the author. Even without it, the pattern of "type first, validator derived" is worth adopting over hand-written schemas.

signals.title_or_quote: How to increase type-safety when generically indexing into generic types
signals.why_relevant: TypeScript developer seeking stronger type safety at runtime boundaries — schemaguard addresses this by compiling validators from types.
signals.drafted_reply: For generic indexing type safety, the compile-time constraints you have are the right tool. At runtime boundaries (API responses, JSON parsing) you also need a validator that matches those same constraints — and keeping a hand-written Zod schema in sync with generic types is fragile. One option is to compile the validator from the type itself. schemaguard ({APP_URL}) does this at build time. Disclosure: I built it. The accepted answer here covers the static side well; this is the runtime complement.

rescore.why: The thread is about TypeScript compile-time type inference for generic lens constructors, not about runtime validation or schema duplication — the app's core problem.
